claims.text: The register must contain details of the systems where customer data are stored.
quotes: details of systems where customer data are stored

claims.text: The register must contain the associated business applications, if any.
quotes: associated business applications, if any

claims.text: The register must record the criticality of the systems, for example high, medium or low.
quotes: criticality of the systems (for example, high / medium / low)

claims.text: A small finance bank's Board must fulfil four major roles: overseeing the bank's risk profile, monitoring the integrity of its business and control mechanisms, ensuring expert management, and maximising the interests of its stakeholders.
quotes: A bank’s Board shall fulfil four major roles viz. overseeing the risk profile of the bank, monitoring the integrity of its business and control mechanisms, ensuring the expert management, and maximising the interests of its stakeholders.

claims.text: The Board must set and enforce clear lines of responsibility and accountability for itself, senior management and the whole organisation.
quotes: set and enforce clear lines of responsibility and accountability for itself as well as the senior management and throughout the organization

claims.text: The Board must pay specific attention to creating and sustaining a culture of control.
quotes: The Board shall specifically pay attention to creating and sustaining a culture of control.

claims.text: The Board must maintain oversight of the bank's risk management system, policy and strategy, its exposures to related entities, and its conformity with corporate governance standards.
quotes: risk management system, policy and strategy followed by the bank
exposures to related entities of the bank
conformity with corporate governance standards

claims.text: The Board must ensure that directors' responsibilities are well-defined and that every director is familiarised with the bank's functioning before induction.
quotes: ensure that responsibilities of its directors are well-defined, and every director is familiarised with the functioning of the bank before their induction

claims.text: The Board is responsible for approving policies and for risk governance in respect of the various activities the bank undertakes.
quotes: responsible for approval of policies and risk governance in respect of various activities undertaken by the bank

claims.text: For projects where financial closure was achieved as on October 1, 2025, any resolution of a fresh credit event and/or change in material terms and conditions in the loan contract on or after October 1, 2025, is governed by the guidelines in paragraphs 101 to 119 of the Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions.
quotes: any resolution of a fresh credit event and/or change in material terms and conditions in the loan contract in such projects, on or after October 1, 2025, shall be as per the guidelines contained in paragraphs 101 to 119.
projects where financial closure has been achieved as on October 1, 2025

claims.text: In such a resolution, the provisioning provisions of paragraph 115 apply to these projects as if they were sanctioned on or after October 1, 2025.
quotes: in case of any resolution of a fresh credit event and / or change in material terms and conditions in the loan contract in such projects, the provisions stipulated in paragraph 115 shall apply to these projects as if these were sanctioned on or after October 1, 2025.

claims.text: Under these guidelines, the AIFI must monitor the project's performance and any buildup of stress on an ongoing basis and is expected to initiate a resolution plan well in advance.
quotes: An AIFI shall monitor the performance of the project and any buildup of stress on an ongoing basis and shall be expected to initiate a resolution plan well in advance.

claims.text: Provisioning for project loans classified as standard or NPA is as per the Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions.
quotes: Provisioning for project loans classified as ‘standard’ (construction or operational phase) or NPA shall be as per extant instructions contained in the Reserve Bank of India (All India Financial Institutions – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025.

claims.text: An ARC must classify a non-performing asset as a loss asset if it has been non-performing for a period exceeding 36 months.
quotes: 'Loss asset' if-
the asset is non-performing for a period exceeding 36 months

claims.text: It must also be classified as a loss asset if it is adversely affected by a potential threat of non-recoverability due to erosion in the value of security or non-availability of security.
quotes: the asset is adversely affected by a potential threat of non-recoverability due to either erosion in the value of security or non-availability of security

claims.text: It must be classified as a loss asset if it has been identified as a loss asset by the ARC or its internal or external auditor.
quotes: the asset has been identified as a loss asset by the ARC or its internal or external auditor

claims.text: It must be classified as a loss asset if the financial asset, including security receipts, is not realised within the total time frame in the ARC's realisation plan under paragraph 36 and the ARC or trust continues to hold it.
quotes: the financial asset including SRs is not realized within the total time frame specified in the plan for realisation formulated by the ARC under paragraph 36 and the ARC or the trust concerned continues to hold those assets

claims.text: Under paragraph 36, the realisation period must not exceed five years from acquisition, though the Board may extend the total period to no more than eight years from acquisition.
quotes: the period for realisation shall not exceed five years from the date of acquisition of the financial asset concerned
the total period for realisation shall not exceed eight years from the date of acquisition of the financial asset concerned

claims.text: A loss asset must be written off entirely; if it is retained in the books, 100 percent provision is required.
quotes: The entire asset shall be written off
If, for any reason, the asset is retained in the books, 100 percent thereof shall be provided for

claims.text: The reporting ARC is responsible for reporting correct information and for ensuring the accuracy of the facts and figures.
quotes: The responsibility for reporting correct information and also ensuring the accuracy of facts and figures rests with the reporting ARC.

claims.text: When furnishing information to credit information companies, the ARC must ensure the accuracy of the directors' particulars, wherever possible by cross-checking them with the database maintained by the Registrar of Companies.
quotes: An ARC, while furnishing information to credit information companies, shall ensure the accuracy of the particulars of the directors, and wherever possible, by cross-checking with the database maintained by the Registrar of Companies.

claims.text: A credit information company must periodically review the financial and operational condition of each service provider to assess whether it can continue to meet its obligations, and it must use a risk-based approach to set how often these reviews happen.
quotes: A CIC shall periodically review the financial and operational condition of the service provider to assess its ability to continue to meet its obligations.
A CIC shall adopt risk-based approach in defining the periodicity.

claims.text: These due diligence reviews must highlight any deterioration or breach in performance standards, confidentiality, security and operational resilience preparedness.
quotes: Such due diligence reviews shall highlight any deterioration or breach in performance standards, confidentiality, security, and operational resilience preparedness.

claims.text: Separately, the company must conduct regular audits of its service providers, including sub-contractors, and the frequency of those audits is set by the nature and extent of the risk and the impact of the outsourcing arrangement on the company.
quotes: A CIC shall conduct regular audits
of service providers (including sub-contractors)
The frequency of the audit shall be determined based on the nature and extent of risk, and impact on the CIC from the outsourcing arrangements.

claims.text: Senior Management must review reports on monitoring and control activities periodically, and any adverse development must be put up to the Board for information.
quotes: Reports on the monitoring and control activities shall be reviewed periodically by the Senior Management, and in case of any adverse development, the same shall be put up to the Board for information.

claims.text: A mortgage guarantee company must classify its assets, loans and advances and any other forms of credit into four classes: standard assets, sub-standard assets, doubtful assets and loss assets.
quotes: classify its assets, loans and advances and any other forms of credit into the following classes, namely:
(1) Standard assets;
(2) Sub-standard assets;
(3) Doubtful assets; and
(4) Loss assets

claims.text: The classification is made after taking into account the degree of well defined credit weaknesses and the extent of dependence on collateral security for realisation.
quotes: after taking into account the degree of well defined credit weaknesses and extent of dependence on collateral security for realisation

claims.text: Assets acquired under guarantee obligations are not to be classified as standard assets.
quotes: Assets acquired under guarantee obligations will not be classified as standard assets.

claims.text: An asset's class is not to be upgraded merely because of rescheduling, unless it satisfies the conditions the Reserve Bank stipulates for upgradation.
quotes: shall not be upgraded merely as a result of rescheduling, unless it satisfies the conditions as stipulated by the Reserve Bank from time to time

claims.text: A housing finance company must record on the face of fixed deposit receipts (and RD passbooks) whether the nomination facility has been availed, using the legend "Nomination Registered".
quotes: The HFC shall introduce the practice of recording on the face of the RD passbooks/ FDRs the position regarding availment of nomination facility with the legend “Nomination Registered”

claims.text: It must also indicate the name of the nominee on the fixed deposit receipt, if the customer agrees to this.
quotes: they shall also indicate the name of the Nominee in the RD passbook/ FDRs, in case the customer is agreeable to the same

claims.text: A payments bank's net cumulative negative mismatches in the domestic Structural Liquidity Statement must not exceed 5 per cent of cumulative cash outflows in the next-day bucket, 10 per cent in the 2-7 days bucket, 15 per cent in the 8-14 days bucket, and 20 per cent in the 15-30 days bucket.
quotes: The net cumulative negative mismatches in the domestic SLS (Refer Annex-I - Part A1 Liquidity Return) during the next day, 2-7 days, 8-14 days, and 15-30 days bucket shall not exceed 5 per cent, 10 per cent, 15 per cent, and 20 per cent of the cumulative cash outflows in the respective time bucket.

claims.text: The bank must also adopt the same cumulative mismatch limits for its Structural Liquidity Statement covering consolidated bank operations.
quotes: A bank shall also adopt the above cumulative mismatch limits for its SLS for consolidated bank operations (Annex-I – Part B).

claims.text: The main focus is on short-term mismatches up to 30 days, and the bank must also monitor cumulative mismatches across all time buckets by setting internal prudential limits approved by the Board or the Risk Management Committee.
quotes: the main focus shall be on the short-term mismatches, i.e., up to 30 days
A bank shall also monitor cumulative mismatches across all time buckets by setting internal prudential limits, with the approval of the Board or the RMC.

claims.text: For critical information systems and/or those in the DMZ having a customer interface, vulnerability assessment must be conducted at least once every six months and penetration testing at least once in 12 months.
quotes: For critical information systems and / or those in the DMZ having customer interface, VA shall be conducted at least once in every six months and PT at least once in 12 months.

claims.text: For non-critical information systems, the bank must use a risk-based approach to decide whether and how often to conduct vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.
quotes: For non-critical information systems, a risk-based approach shall be adopted to decide the requirement and periodicity of conduct of VA / PT.

claims.text: Vulnerability assessment and penetration testing of critical, internet-facing applications, servers and network components must also be done throughout their lifecycle, including pre-implementation, post-implementation and after changes.
quotes: periodically conduct VA / PT of critical, internet facing web / mobile applications, servers, and network components throughout their lifecycle including pre-implementation, post-implementation, and after changes

claims.text: A drawn tranche of an AIFI's contingent partial credit enhancement facility must be repaid within 30 days from the date it was drawn; that date is the due date.
quotes: a drawn tranche of the contingent PCE facility shall be required to be repaid within 30 days from the date of its drawal (due date)

claims.text: The facility is treated as an NPA if it remains outstanding for 90 days or more from the due date, and it is provided for under the usual asset classification and provisioning norms.
quotes: The facility shall be treated as NPA if it remains outstanding for 90 days or more from the due date and provided for as per the usual asset classification and provisioning norms.

claims.text: When that happens, the AIFI's other facilities to the borrower are also classified as NPA under extant guidelines.
quotes: In that event, the AIFIs’ other facilities to the borrower shall also be classified as NPA as per extant guidelines.

claims.text: The short repayment period applies because a credit enhancement is drawn only when there is a cash flow shortfall for servicing a debt or bond, which indicates that the project is in financial distress.

such an event is indicative of financial distress of the project

claims.text: For a rating to be eligible for risk weighting, the rating agency should have reviewed it at least once during the previous 15 months.
quotes: The rating agency should have reviewed the rating at least once during the previous 15 months.

claims.text: The rating must also be in force and confirmed from the monthly bulletin of the rating agency concerned.
quotes: the rating shall be in force and confirmed from the monthly bulletin of the concerned rating agency

claims.text: Every commercial bank must maintain in India SLR assets whose value, at the close of business on any day, is not less than 18 per cent of its total net demand and time liabilities in India as on the last day of the second preceding fortnight.
quotes: Every bank shall maintain in India assets (hereinafter referred to as 'SLR assets') the value of which shall not, at the close of business on any day, be less than 18 per cent of its total net demand and time liabilities in India as on the last day of the second preceding fortnight

claims.text: The SLR assets are valued using the method of valuation specified by RBI from time to time.
quotes: in accordance with the method of valuation specified by RBI from time to time

claims.text: SLR is maintained in addition to the cash reserves a bank must keep, and the percentage the Reserve Bank may specify cannot exceed 40 percent of the bank's demand and time liabilities in India.
quotes: in addition to the cash reserves which it is required to maintain under these Directions
such percentage not exceeding 40 percent of the total of its demand and time liabilities in India

claims.text: Yes. Interest on domestic rupee savings deposits is calculated on a daily product basis, and a payments bank may provide differential rates of interest for any end-of-day savings account balance exceeding ₹1 lakh.
quotes: Interest shall be calculated on a daily product basis
Differential rates of interest may be provided for any end-of-day savings bank account balance exceeding ₹1 lakh.

claims.text: On balances up to ₹1 lakh, a uniform interest rate must be set, irrespective of the amount in the account within that limit.
quotes: A uniform interest rate shall be set on balance up to ₹1 lakh, irrespective of the amount in the account within this limit.

claims.text: A payments bank can hold a maximum end-of-day balance of ₹2,00,000 per individual customer.

claims.text: This statutory limit is an aggregate holding limit for each company, and shares held in demat form are included.

quotes: The aggregate equity investments made in all entities, including overseas investments, shall not exceed 20 per cent of the bank’s paid-up share capital and reserves

claims.text: An investment of 20 percent or more in an entity's equity share capital requires prior approval of the Reserve Bank.
quotes: A bank, with prior approval of the Reserve Bank, may make an aggregate investment of 20 percent or more in the equity share capital of an entity.

acquisition is through restructuring of debt or to protect the banks’ interest on loans/investments made to an entity

quotes: A Scheduled UCB, shall be eligible to provide online trading facility to its demat account holders by entering into a tie-up with a broking entity with prior approval of the RBI

claims.text: Its assessed net worth must be at least ₹500 crore as per its last inspection report.

quotes: A UCB shall be Financially Sound and Well Managed, as per criteria prescribed in our Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks - Branch Authorisation) Directions, 2025

claims.text: It must be registered with SEBI as a Depository Participant.

claims.text: It must have fully implemented Core Banking Solutions and be offering Internet Banking to its customers.
quotes: A UCB shall have fully implemented Core Banking Solutions (CBS) and shall be offering Internet Banking services to its customers.

claims.text: Its Board must pass a resolution confirming the bank will not offer investment tips or recommendations to customers nor undertake portfolio management services.
quotes: shall pass a resolution confirming that the UCB shall not offer investment tips or recommendations to customers, nor undertake portfolio management services

claims.text: The bank must apply through the PRAVAAH Portal to the RBI's Department of Regulation, attaching a copy of that Board Resolution.
quotes: shall submit its application through PRAVAAH Portal (https://pravaah.rbi.org.in) to Department of Regulation, RBI with a copy of Board Resolution

claims.text: For accounts with aggregate exposure above a specified threshold with the specified lenders on or after the reference date, the resolution plan must be implemented within 180 days from the end of the Review Period.

claims.text: The Review Period commences no later than the reference date if the account is in default on that date, or otherwise the date of first default after the reference date.
quotes: the reference date, if in default as on the reference date; or
the date of first default after the reference date.

claims.text: The reference date is June 07, 2019 for aggregate exposure of ₹2000 crore and above, and January 1, 2020 for exposure of ₹1500 crore and above but less than ₹2000 crore; for exposure below ₹1500 crore it is to be announced in due course.

₹1500 crore and above, but less than ₹2000 crore | January 1, 2020
Less than ₹1500 crore | To be announced in due course

quotes: 365 days from the commencement of Review Period | 15 per cent (i.e. total additional provisioning of 35 per cent)

quotes: invoked no later than 45 days from the date of the declaration of calamity and shall be implemented within 135 days from the date of the declaration

claims.text: Interest on FCNR(B) deposits is calculated and paid at intervals of 180 days each, and thereafter for the remaining actual number of days.
quotes: The interest on FCNR (B) deposits shall be calculated and paid at intervals of 180 days each and thereafter for the remaining actual number of days.

claims.text: The depositor may instead choose to receive the interest on maturity with compounding effect.
quotes: the option to receive the interest on maturity with compounding effect shall vest with the depositor

claims.text: The interest is calculated on the basis of 360 days to a year.
quotes: Interest on the deposits accepted under the Scheme shall be calculated on the basis of 360 days to a year.

claims.text: The banking company must furnish its comments to the Reserve Bank within 30 days of receiving the Reserve Bank's reference on the proposed acquisition.
quotes: shall furnish its comments to the Reserve Bank
within 30 days of receipt of the reference from the Reserve Bank

claims.text: The comments must come after considering all relevant aspects, and must be accompanied by a copy of the relevant board resolution and information in Form A1.
quotes: after considering all relevant aspects, along with a copy of the relevant board resolution and information in Form A1

claims.text: Before responding, the bank's Board must deliberate on the proposed acquisition and assess the 'fit and proper' status of the person, based on the information provided and the bank's own due diligence.

claims.text: An NBFC must prepare its balance sheet and profit and loss account, as prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013, as on March 31 every year.
quotes: An NBFC shall prepare its balance sheet and profit and loss account, as prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013, as on March 31 every year.

claims.text: Every NBFC must finalise its balance sheet within 3 months from the date to which it pertains.
quotes: Every NBFC shall finalise its balance sheet within a period of 3 months from the date to which it pertains.

claims.text: If an NBFC intends to extend the date of its balance sheet under the Companies Act, 2013, it must take prior approval of the Reserve Bank before approaching the Registrar of Companies.

NBFCs designated as NBFC-UL in the previous year.
NBFCs added to the set by supervisors using supervisory judgment.

claims.text: Scores of all NBFCs in that set are computed annually based on their position as on March 31 each year.

claims.text: The quantitative parameters are size and leverage, interconnectedness, and complexity; the qualitative parameters / supervisory inputs are nature and type of liabilities, group structure, and segment penetration.
quotes: Size & Leverage
Interconnectedness
Complexity
Nature and type of liabilities
Group Structure
Segment Penetration

claims.text: The Upper Layer comprises NBFCs that the Reserve Bank specifically identifies annually as warranting enhanced regulatory requirement.

claims.text: The identification is based on the criteria set out in paragraph 24 of the Directions. The text of paragraph 24 is not among the paragraphs provided, so the criteria themselves cannot be stated here.

claims.text: This statement is in addition to the matter in Paragraph 6(1), under which the auditor examines whether a company engaged in the business of a non-banking financial institution has obtained a Certificate of Registration from RBI.
quotes: Apart from the matters enumerated in Paragraph 6(1) above
the auditor of the NBFC shall examine whether the company has obtained a CoR from RBI.

claims.text: A commercial bank must follow a 'secure by design' approach in developing digital payment products and services.
quotes: The bank shall follow a ‘secure by design’ approach in the development of digital payment products and services.

claims.text: The bank must ensure digital payment applications are inherently more secure by embedding security within their development lifecycle.
quotes: The bank shall ensure that digital payment applications are inherently more secure by embedding security within their development lifecycle.

claims.text: The bank must also have a Board-approved policy for digital payment products and services that explicitly covers payment security requirements from Functionality, Security and Performance (FSP) angles.
quotes: The bank shall formulate a policy for digital payment products and services with the approval of its Board.
shall explicitly cover payment security requirements from Functionality, Security and Performance (FSP) angles

claims.text: These requirements include assurance that the payment product is built securely and rolled out after necessary testing to achieve the desired FSP.
quotes: assurance that the payment product is built in a secure manner offering robust performance ensuring safety, consistency, and rolled out after necessary testing for achieving desired FSP

claims.text: When a rural co-operative bank transfers a stressed loan to an ARC at a price below its net book value (NBV) at the time of transfer, it must debit the shortfall to the profit and loss account for the year in which the transfer took place.
quotes: When the stressed loan is transferred to ARC at a price below the NBV at the time of transfer, bank shall debit the shortfall to the profit and loss account for the year in which the transfer has taken place.

claims.text: The bank may use countercyclical or floating provisions to meet any such shortfall.
quotes: A bank is permitted to use countercyclical or floating provisions for meeting any shortfall on transfer of stressed loan when the transfer is at a price below the NBV.

claims.text: Yes. A small finance bank must report to credit information companies the details of guarantors who have failed to honour their commitments when the guarantee is invoked.
quotes: A bank shall report to credit information companies the details of guarantors who have failed to honour the commitments thereunder when invoked

claims.text: Such guarantors are to be reported as large defaulters or wilful defaulters, as the case may be.
quotes: as large defaulters / wilful defaulters, as the case may be

claims.text: The details are to be reported as per Annex I and II.
quotes: The details shall be reported as per Annex I and II.

claims.text: For the portion up to 5 per cent of the book value of loans being securitised, the originator must retain the MRR first through a first loss facility, if available.
quotes: Up to 5 per cent of the book value of loans being securitised:
First loss facility, if available;

claims.text: If no first loss facility is available, or the entire first loss facility amounts to less than 5 per cent, the balance must be retained through the equity tranche.
quotes: If first loss facility is not available, or where retention of the entire first loss facility amounts to less than 5 per cent, balance through retention of equity tranche;

claims.text: Where the first loss facility and equity tranche together amount to less than 5 per cent, the balance must be held pari passu in the remaining tranches sold to investors.
quotes: Where retention of the entire first loss facility, if available, and equity tranche amounts to less than 5 per cent, balance pari passu in remaining tranches sold to investors.

claims.text: For retention greater than 5 per cent of the book value, the MRR may be held through the first loss facility, the equity tranche or any other tranche sold to investors, in any combination.
quotes: Greater than 5 per cent of the book value of loans being securitised:
First loss facility, or equity tranche or any other tranche sold to investors, in any combination thereof.

claims.text: Overcollateralisation does not count as a first loss facility for this purpose.
quotes: first loss facility for this purpose shall not include overcollateralization available, if any.

claims.text: Investment in the Interest Only Strip representing the Excess Interest Spread or Future Margin Income does not count towards the MRR.
quotes: Investment in the Interest Only Strip representing the Excess Interest Spread/ Future Margin Income, whether or not subordinated, will not be counted towards the MRR.

claims.text: The MRR must be maintained by the originating bank itself, not by any group entity, and its form must not change during the life of the securitisation.
quotes: MRR has to be maintained by the originating bank itself and not by any of its group entities. The form of MRR should not change during the life of securitisation.

claims.text: The MRR must not be reduced by hedging credit risk or by selling or encumbering the retained interest.
quotes: MRR should not be reduced either through hedging of credit risk or selling or encumbering the retained interest.

claims.text: The MRR, as a percentage of unamortised principal, must be maintained on an ongoing basis, except for reductions due to repayment or loss absorption; where there is a replenishment period, it must also be maintained at the end of that period.
quotes: The MRR as a percentage of unamortised principal should be maintained on an ongoing basis except for reduction of retained exposure due to repayment or through the absorption of losses.
MRR should be maintained not only at the initiation of the securitisation but also at the end of the replenishment period.

claims.text: The bank must ensure proper documentation in accordance with law for complying with the MRR.
quotes: bank should ensure that proper documentation in accordance with law is made.

claims.text: When a commercial bank outsources services, responsibility for redressing customers' grievances related to the outsourced services rests with the bank, and its grievance redressal mechanism must not be compromised in any way because of the outsourcing.
quotes: A bank shall have a robust grievance redressal mechanism that shall not be compromised in any manner on account of outsourcing
responsibility for redressal of customers’ grievances related to outsourced services shall rest with the bank

claims.text: For microfinance loans, the bank must declare that it is accountable for inappropriate behaviour of the service provider's employees.
quotes: In case of microfinance loans, a declaration that, (i) the bank shall be accountable for inappropriate behaviour of the employees of the service provider

claims.text: For microfinance loans, the bank must also declare that it will provide timely grievance redressal.
quotes: (ii) shall provide timely grievance redressal

claims.text: These declarations must be made in the loan agreement and in the Fair Practices Code displayed in the bank's office, its branch premises and its website.
quotes: shall be made in the loan agreement, and in Fair Practices Code (FPC) displayed in its office, branch premises, and its website

claims.text: Outsourcing does not affect customers' rights against the bank, including their ability to obtain redressal under relevant laws.
quotes: Outsourcing arrangements entered into by a bank shall not affect the rights of its customers against the bank, including the ability of the customers to obtain redressal as applicable under relevant laws.

claims.text: The UCB must notify customers directly and also publicise the benefits of the nomination facility through various media, including periodical drives aimed at full coverage of all eligible customer accounts.
quotes: in addition to directly notifying the customers, shall publicise the benefits of using the nomination facility through various media, including launching periodical drives towards achieving a full coverage of all eligible customer accounts

claims.text: It must give wide publicity and guidance on the benefits of nomination to deposit account holders, locker hirers and depositors of articles in safe custody. This may include printing messages on cheque books, passbooks and other customer literature, and running periodical awareness drives.
quotes: A UCB shall give wide publicity and provide guidance to deposit account holders, locker hirers and depositors of articles in safe custody on the benefits of the nomination facility.
printing compatible messages on cheque book, passbook and other literature reaching the customers as well as launching periodical awareness drives

claims.text: It must suitably sensitise its frontline branch staff to obtaining nominations, handling claims of deceased constituents, and dealing with nominees or legal heirs.
quotes: shall suitably sensitise its frontline staff in the branches for obtaining nomination as well as appropriate handling of claims of deceased constituents and dealing with nominees / legal heirs

claims.text: Account opening forms must be modified, if this has not already been done, so that customers can either avail of or opt out of the nomination facility.
quotes: shall modify the Account Opening Forms suitably (if not already done) with provision for the customers to avail or opt out of nomination facility

claims.text: Forms for opening deposit accounts, hiring lockers and depositing articles in safe custody must contain a space for nomination details. This also serves to make customers aware that the facility is available.
quotes: contains a space for getting the details of nomination, which also serves the purpose of educating the customers about availability of such facility

claims.text: A small finance bank must provide its internal audit department (IAD) with appropriate resources and staff to achieve its objectives under the risk-based internal audit (RBIA) system.
quotes: The bank shall provide appropriate resources and staff to the IAD to achieve its objectives under the RBIA system.

claims.text: Internal auditors should be trained periodically so they understand the bank's business activities, operating procedures, risk management and control systems, and Management Information System.
quotes: They should also be trained periodically to enable them to understand the bank’s business activities, operating procedures, risk management and control systems, and Management Information System (MIS).

claims.text: The bank must ensure that its internal audit function has the requisite skills to audit all areas of the bank.
quotes: The bank shall ensure that its Internal Audit function has the requisite skills to audit all areas of the bank.

claims.text: A commercial bank must invoke the default loss guarantee (DLG) within a maximum overdue period of 120 days, unless the borrower makes good the loan dues before that.
quotes: A bank shall invoke DLG within a maximum overdue period of 120 days, unless the loan dues are made good by the borrower before that.

claims.text: The DLG agreement must remain in force for a period not less than the longest tenor of the loan in the underlying loan portfolio.
quotes: The period for which the DLG agreement remains in force shall not be less than the longest tenor of the loan in the underlying loan portfolio.

claims.text: An urban co-operative bank must maintain an up-to-date information asset inventory register that contains, at a minimum, the fields listed below.
quotes: The UCB shall maintain an up-to-date information asset inventory register containing the following fields, as a minimum:

claims.text: The register must include details of the information asset, such as hardware, software, network devices, key personnel and services.
quotes: details of the information asset (such as hardware / software / network devices, key personnel, services)

claims.text: The register must include details of the systems where customer data are stored.
quotes: details of systems where customer data are stored

claims.text: The register must include the associated business applications, if any.
quotes: associated business applications, if any

claims.text: The register must include the criticality of the systems, for example high, medium or low.
quotes: criticality of the systems (for example, high / medium / low)

claims.text: Under paragraph 17 of the Small Finance Banks Governance Directions, a small finance bank's Board must fulfil four major roles: overseeing the bank's risk profile, monitoring the integrity of its business and control mechanisms, ensuring expert management, and maximising the interests of its stakeholders.
quotes: A bank’s Board shall fulfil four major roles viz. overseeing the risk profile of the bank, monitoring the integrity of its business and control mechanisms, ensuring the expert management, and maximising the interests of its stakeholders.

claims.text: The Board must also ensure that its directors' responsibilities are well-defined and that every director is familiarised with how the bank functions before their induction.
quotes: The Board of a bank shall ensure that responsibilities of its directors are well-defined, and every director is familiarised with the functioning of the bank before their induction

claims.text: The Board is responsible for approving policies and for risk governance for the various activities the bank undertakes.
quotes: The Board of a bank shall be responsible for approval of policies and risk governance in respect of various activities undertaken by the bank.

claims.text: For projects under implementation, an AIFI's resolution of a fresh credit event and/or change in material terms and conditions in the loan contract on or after October 1, 2025 must follow the guidelines in paragraphs 101 to 119, notwithstanding paragraph 99.
quotes: Notwithstanding the instructions in paragraph 99, any resolution of a fresh credit event and/or change in material terms and conditions in the loan contract in such projects, on or after October 1, 2025, shall be as per the guidelines contained in paragraphs 101 to 119.

claims.text: Notwithstanding paragraph 117, in such a resolution the provisions in paragraph 115 apply to these projects as if they had been sanctioned on or after October 1, 2025.
quotes: Notwithstanding the instructions in paragraph 117, in case of any resolution of a fresh credit event and / or change in material terms and conditions in the loan contract in such projects, the provisions stipulated in paragraph 115 shall apply to these projects as if these were sanctioned on or after October 1, 2025.

claims.text: Under paragraph 97, a non-performing asset must be classified as a loss asset if it has been non-performing for a period exceeding 36 months.
quotes: 'Loss asset' if-
the asset is non-performing for a period exceeding 36 months

claims.text: It must also be classified as a loss asset if it is adversely affected by a potential threat of non-recoverability due to erosion in the value of security or non-availability of security.
quotes: the asset is adversely affected by a potential threat of non-recoverability due to either erosion in the value of security or non-availability of security

claims.text: It must be classified as a loss asset if the ARC or its internal or external auditor has identified it as a loss asset.
quotes: the asset has been identified as a loss asset by the ARC or its internal or external auditor

claims.text: It must be classified as a loss asset if the financial asset, including security receipts, is not realised within the total time frame in the ARC's realisation plan under paragraph 36 and the ARC or trust continues to hold those assets.
quotes: the financial asset including SRs is not realized within the total time frame specified in the plan for realisation formulated by the ARC under paragraph 36 and the ARC or the trust concerned continues to hold those assets

claims.text: Under paragraph 36, the realisation period may not exceed five years from acquisition of the financial asset, though the Board may extend it so the total does not exceed eight years.
quotes: the period for realisation shall not exceed five years from the date of acquisition of the financial asset concerned
the total period for realisation shall not exceed eight years from the date of acquisition

claims.text: The reporting ARC is responsible for reporting correct information on wilful and large defaulters and for ensuring the accuracy of the facts and figures.
quotes: The responsibility for reporting correct information and also ensuring the accuracy of facts and figures rests with the reporting ARC.

claims.text: When furnishing information to credit information companies, the ARC must ensure the accuracy of directors' particulars, cross-checking them with the Registrar of Companies database wherever possible.
quotes: while furnishing information to credit information companies, shall ensure the accuracy of the particulars of the directors, and wherever possible, by cross-checking with the database maintained by the Registrar of Companies

claims.text: A credit information company must periodically review the financial and operational condition of each service provider to assess its ability to continue meeting its obligations, and must use a risk-based approach to decide how often those reviews happen.
quotes: A CIC shall periodically review the financial and operational condition of the service provider to assess its ability to continue to meet its obligations.
A CIC shall adopt risk-based approach in defining the periodicity.

claims.text: These due diligence reviews must highlight any deterioration or breach in performance standards, confidentiality, security, and operational resilience preparedness.
quotes: Such due diligence reviews shall highlight any deterioration or breach in performance standards, confidentiality, security, and operational resilience preparedness.

claims.text: Separately, the company must conduct regular audits of service providers, including sub-contractors. How often these audits happen is set by the nature and extent of the risk and the impact of the outsourcing arrangements on the company.
quotes: A CIC shall conduct regular audits (as applicable to the scope of these Directions) of service providers (including sub-contractors)
The frequency of the audit shall be determined based on the nature and extent of risk, and impact on the CIC from the outsourcing arrangements.

claims.text: Senior Management must review reports on monitoring and control activities periodically, and any adverse development must be put up to the Board for information.
quotes: Reports on the monitoring and control activities shall be reviewed periodically by the Senior Management, and in case of any adverse development, the same shall be put up to the Board for information.

claims.text: A mortgage guarantee company must classify its assets, loans and advances and any other forms of credit into four classes: standard assets, sub-standard assets, doubtful assets and loss assets.
quotes: classify its assets, loans and advances and any other forms of credit into the following classes
(1) Standard assets;
(2) Sub-standard assets;
(3) Doubtful assets; and
(4) Loss assets

claims.text: The classification is made after taking into account the degree of well defined credit weaknesses and the extent of dependence on collateral security for realisation.
quotes: after taking into account the degree of well defined credit weaknesses and extent of dependence on collateral security for realisation

claims.text: Assets acquired under guarantee obligations are not to be classified as standard assets.
quotes: Assets acquired under guarantee obligations will not be classified as standard assets.

claims.text: A housing finance company must record on the face of fixed deposit receipts (and RD passbooks) whether the nomination facility has been availed, using the legend "Nomination Registered".
quotes: The HFC shall introduce the practice of recording on the face of the RD passbooks/ FDRs the position regarding availment of nomination facility with the legend “Nomination Registered”

claims.text: It must also indicate the name of the nominee on the fixed deposit receipts, if the customer agrees to this.
quotes: they shall also indicate the name of the Nominee in the RD passbook/ FDRs, in case the customer is agreeable to the same

claims.text: A payments bank's net cumulative negative mismatches in the domestic Structural Liquidity Statement shall not exceed 5 per cent of cumulative cash outflows in the next day bucket, 10 per cent in the 2-7 days bucket, 15 per cent in the 8-14 days bucket and 20 per cent in the 15-30 days bucket.
quotes: The net cumulative negative mismatches in the domestic SLS (Refer Annex-I - Part A1 Liquidity Return) during the next day, 2-7 days, 8-14 days, and 15-30 days bucket shall not exceed 5 per cent, 10 per cent, 15 per cent, and 20 per cent of the cumulative cash outflows in the respective time bucket.

claims.text: The bank must also adopt the same cumulative mismatch limits for its Structural Liquidity Statement for consolidated bank operations.
quotes: A bank shall also adopt the above cumulative mismatch limits for its SLS for consolidated bank operations (Annex-I – Part B).

claims.text: A small finance bank must conduct vulnerability assessment and penetration testing exercises periodically for all critical and internet-facing systems.
quotes: The bank shall conduct VA and PT exercises periodically for all the critical and internet facing systems.

claims.text: For critical information systems and/or those in the DMZ having a customer interface, vulnerability assessment must be conducted at least once every six months.
quotes: For critical information systems and / or those in the DMZ having customer interface, VA shall be conducted at least once in every six months

claims.text: For those same critical systems, penetration testing must be conducted at least once in 12 months.
quotes: PT at least once in 12 months

claims.text: For non-critical information systems, the bank must take a risk-based approach to decide whether vulnerability assessment and penetration testing are needed and how often.
quotes: For non-critical information systems, a risk-based approach shall be adopted to decide the requirement and periodicity of conduct of VA / PT.

claims.text: A drawn tranche of an AIFI's contingent partial credit enhancement facility must be repaid within 30 days from the date it was drawn, which is its due date.
quotes: a drawn tranche of the contingent PCE facility shall be required to be repaid within 30 days from the date of its drawal (due date)

claims.text: The facility is treated as an NPA if it remains outstanding for 90 days or more from the due date, and is provided for under the usual asset classification and provisioning norms.
quotes: The facility shall be treated as NPA if it remains outstanding for 90 days or more from the due date and provided for as per the usual asset classification and provisioning norms

claims.text: When that happens, the AIFI's other facilities to the borrower are also classified as NPA under extant guidelines.
quotes: other facilities to the borrower shall also be classified as NPA as per extant guidelines

claims.text: This treatment reflects that credit enhancement is drawn only when there is a cash flow shortfall in servicing debt, which indicates financial distress of the project.
quotes: Credit Enhancement (CE) gets drawn only in a contingent situation of cash flow shortfall for servicing a debt / bond etc.
such an event is indicative of financial distress of the project

claims.text: For a rating to be eligible for risk weighting purposes, the rating agency should have reviewed it at least once during the previous 15 months.
quotes: The rating agency should have reviewed the rating at least once during the previous 15 months.

claims.text: The rating must also be in force and confirmed from the monthly bulletin of the concerned rating agency.
quotes: the rating shall be in force and confirmed from the monthly bulletin of the concerned rating agency

claims.text: Every commercial bank must maintain SLR assets in India whose value, at the close of business on any day, is not less than 18 per cent of its total net demand and time liabilities in India.
quotes: the value of which shall not, at the close of business on any day, be less than 18 per cent of its total net demand and time liabilities in India

claims.text: The liabilities are measured as on the last day of the second preceding fortnight, and the assets are valued by the method RBI specifies from time to time.
quotes: as on the last day of the second preceding fortnight in accordance with the method of valuation specified by RBI from time to time

claims.text: The SLR is maintained in addition to the cash reserves the bank must keep, and the Reserve Bank may specify the percentage by notification in the Official Gazette, up to a ceiling of 40 percent.
quotes: in addition to the cash reserves which it is required to maintain under these Directions
such percentage not exceeding 40 percent of the total of its demand and time liabilities in India
as the Reserve Bank may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify from time to time

claims.text: Yes. A payments bank may provide differential rates of interest on any end-of-day savings bank account balance exceeding ₹1 lakh.
quotes: Differential rates of interest may be provided for any end-of-day savings bank account balance exceeding ₹1 lakh.

claims.text: On balances up to ₹1 lakh, however, the payments bank must set a uniform interest rate, irrespective of the amount in the account within that limit.
quotes: A uniform interest rate shall be set on balance up to ₹1 lakh, irrespective of the amount in the account within this limit.

claims.text: Interest on savings deposits is calculated on a daily product basis.

claims.text: Separately, a payments bank may hold a maximum end-of-day balance of ₹2,00,000 per individual customer.
quotes: PBs are restricted to holding a maximum balance of ₹2,00,000 per individual customer at the end of the day.

claims.text: Under Section 19(2) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, a small finance bank may not hold shares in any company, whether as pledgee, mortgagee or absolute owner, exceeding 30 per cent of that company's paid-up share capital or 30 per cent of its own paid-up share capital and reserves, whichever is less, except as provided in sub-section (1) of Section 19.
quotes: no banking company shall hold shares in any company, whether as pledgee, mortgagee or absolute owner, of an amount exceeding 30 per cent of the paid-up share capital of that company or 30 per cent of its own paid-up share capital and reserves, whichever is less, except as provided in sub-section (1) of Section 19 of the Act

claims.text: This statutory limit is an aggregate holding limit for each company, and shares held in demat form are included in determining it.
quotes: Shares held in demat form should also be included for the purpose of determining the exposure limit. This is an aggregate holding limit for each company.

claims.text: The bank must strictly adhere to this limit when granting advances against shares, underwriting share issues, or acquiring shares on investment account or in lieu of debt.
quotes: A bank shall strictly adhere to these statutory provisions while granting any advance against shares, underwriting any issue of shares, or acquiring any shares on investment account or even in lieu of debt of any company.

claims.text: Separately, a small finance bank's equity investment in any single entity must not exceed 10 per cent of the bank's paid-up share capital and reserves, as per the last audited balance sheet or the audited/unaudited balance sheet of the latest quarter, whichever is lower.
quotes: Equity investment by a bank in any entity individually, shall not exceed 10 per cent of the bank’s paid-up share capital and reserves as per the last audited balance sheet or audited/unaudited balance sheet of the latest quarter, whichever is lower.

claims.text: A scheduled UCB may provide online trading to its demat account holders only through a tie-up with a broking entity, and only with prior approval of the RBI.
quotes: A Scheduled UCB, shall be eligible to provide online trading facility to its demat account holders by entering into a tie-up with a broking entity with prior approval of the RBI

claims.text: Its assessed net worth must be at least ₹500 crore as per the last inspection report.
quotes: The assessed net worth of the UCB shall not be less than ₹500 crore as per last inspection report

claims.text: It must be Financially Sound and Well Managed under the criteria in the Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025.
quotes: A UCB shall be Financially Sound and Well Managed, as per criteria prescribed in our Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks - Branch Authorisation) Directions, 2025

claims.text: It must be registered with SEBI as a Depository Participant.
quotes: A UCB shall be registered with SEBI as Depository Participant

claims.text: It must have fully implemented Core Banking Solutions and must be offering Internet Banking to its customers.

claims.text: It must apply to the RBI's Department of Regulation through the PRAVAAH Portal.

claims.text: The application must include a copy of a Board Resolution stating that the bank will not offer tips or recommendations to customers for online trading and will not undertake portfolio management services.
quotes: with a copy of Board Resolution to the effect that they shall not be offering tips / recommendations to their customers for on-line trading and shall also not be undertaking portfolio management services

claims.text: Interest on FCNR(B) deposits at an urban co-operative bank is calculated and paid at intervals of 180 days each, and thereafter for the remaining actual number of days.
quotes: The interest on FCNR (B) deposits shall be calculated and paid at intervals of 180 days each and thereafter for the remaining actual number of days.

claims.text: The depositor has the option to receive the interest on maturity with compounding effect instead.
quotes: the option to receive the interest on maturity with compounding effect shall vest with the depositor

claims.text: Interest on these deposits is calculated on the basis of 360 days to a year.
quotes: Interest on the deposits accepted under the Scheme shall be calculated on the basis of 360 days to a year.

claims.text: The bank must furnish its comments to the Reserve Bank within 30 days of receiving the reference from the Reserve Bank.
quotes: within 30 days of receipt of the reference from the Reserve Bank

claims.text: The comments must be given after considering all relevant aspects and must be accompanied by a copy of the relevant board resolution and information in Form A1.
quotes: after considering all relevant aspects, along with a copy of the relevant board resolution and information in Form A1

claims.text: An NBFC must prepare its balance sheet and profit and loss account as on March 31 every year.
quotes: An NBFC shall prepare its balance sheet and profit and loss account, as prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013, as on March 31 every year.

claims.text: Every NBFC must finalise its balance sheet within 3 months from the date to which it pertains.
quotes: Every NBFC shall finalise its balance sheet within a period of 3 months from the date to which it pertains.

claims.text: If an NBFC intends to extend the date of its balance sheet under the Companies Act, 2013, it must take prior approval of the Reserve Bank before approaching the Registrar of Companies.
quotes: Whenever an NBFC intends to extend the date of its balance sheet, as per provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, it shall take prior approval of the Reserve Bank before approaching the Registrar of Companies for this purpose.

claims.text: Even where RBI and the Registrar of Companies grant an extension, the NBFC must furnish to RBI an unaudited proforma balance sheet as on March 31 of the year, along with the statutory returns due on that date.

claims.text: An NBFC accepting or holding public deposits must also deliver to the Reserve Bank its audited balance sheet and profit and loss account, as passed in general meeting, with the Board's report, within fifteen days of that meeting, along with the auditor's report and notes on accounts.

within fifteen days of such meeting as also a copy of the report and the notes on accounts furnished by its Auditor

quotes: The Upper Layer shall comprise of those NBFCs which are specifically identified by the Reserve Bank as warranting enhanced regulatory requirement based on the set of parameters and scoring methodology
